small_guidance:
- The pool+sum kernel is already tiny (16·~5·5·5 outputs); the 11ms is dominated by the ConvTranspose3d. Tuning BLOCK_C / num_warps on the pool kernel will not move the needle — focus tuning effort on the conv. If keeping the pool kernel, try collapsing the 6³ static_range into a single flat static_range of 216 with precomputed (dd,hh,ww) to reduce compiler unroll cost, and bump num_warps to 2 (only 64 channels) with num_stages=2.
- Verify channels_last_3d is actually being honored — the code calls `x.contiguous()` (default layout) right before the pool kernel, which strips the channels_last format possibly set by cuDNN's output. Either keep channels_last throughout or stop forcing contiguous between conv and pool.
large_guidance:
- The ConvTranspose3d dominates runtime (fast_p ≈ 0.95 means we are essentially at cuDNN baseline). Replace it with a custom Triton scatter-add kernel: one program per (N, IC tile, input-spatial tile) computing the outer product `input[n,ic,d,h,w] * weight[ic,oc,kd,kh,kw]` and scatter-adding into output positions `(d*stride - pad + kd, …)`. Fuse the bias add into the same epilogue. With kernel=5, stride=2, padding=2 and OC=64, this is a heavy op with lots of headroom.
- Even better: fuse the transposed conv directly with the 6×6×6 max-pool + channel sum. Since each output of the pool/sum depends on a 6³ window of conv outputs, you can launch one program per (N, od, oh, ow), compute the 6³ conv-transpose output patch on the fly via gather (loop over IC, kd, kh, kw with the inverse index mapping), maintain a per-channel running max across the 216 spatial positions, and reduce across OC at the end. This eliminates the entire ~16·64·64·64·64 intermediate write.
- If full fusion is too complex, at minimum fuse bias+conv_transpose into a custom kernel and keep the existing pool/sum kernel; the conv is where the 5%+ headroom lives.
